cls: Pituitary/placental gonadotropins and ovulation-induction agents (FSH, LH, hCG, hMG; with clomiphene/letrozole as oral ovulation stimulants)
pharm: Group of agents that drive gonadal function - injectable FSH/LH/hMG and chorionic gonadotropin act directly on ovarian (and testicular) gonadotropin receptors to stimulate follicular growth, ovulation and steroidogenesis, while oral ovulation stimulants (clomiphene, letrozole) raise endogenous FSH/LH by reducing estrogen negative feedback.
tags: Risk of OHSS and multiple pregnancy
quick: Highly individualized: FSH/hMG ~75-150 IU/day SC/IM titrated; hCG 5000-10000 IU to trigger; clomiphene 50 mg/day x5 days; letrozole 2.5 mg/day x5 days
Oral agents (clomiphene/letrozole) with or without food; injectables parenteral
Discontinue once pregnancy confirmed; not for use in pregnancy
Caution; clomiphene/letrozole contraindicated in significant hepatic disease
No specific interaction; general moderation advised
Serial ultrasound follicle tracking + serum estradiol, OHSS signs, multiple-pregnancy risk
summary: This is a GROUP entry covering gonadotropins and other ovulation stimulants used in the management of infertility. Injectable agents include follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH, urinary or recombinant follitropin), luteinizing hormone (LH, lutropin), human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG/menotropin, which contains FSH and LH activity), and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG, which mimics the LH surge to trigger final oocyte maturation/ovulation). Oral ovulation stimulants - clomiphene citrate (a selective estrogen receptor modulator) and letrozole (an aromatase inhibitor used off-label/EMA-variable for ovulation induction) - work indirectly by reducing estrogen negative feedback to increase pituitary FSH/LH. These agents are used for ovulation induction in anovulatory infertility (e.g., PCOS), for controlled ovarian stimulation in assisted reproduction, and (gonadotropins/hCG) for selected male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Dosing is highly individualized and titrated to ovarian response under ultrasound and estradiol monitoring. The principal risks across the group are OVARIAN HYPERSTIMULATION SYNDROME (OHSS) and MULTIPLE PREGNANCY, together with thromboembolism, adnexal torsion, and (clomiphene) visual disturbance. Specific products have their own approved labels; this summary uses FDA prescribing information together with EMA/WHO sources for the group.
indications: Ovulation induction in women with anovulatory or oligo-ovulatory infertility (e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome) who are not due to primary ovarian failure
Development of multiple follicles (controlled ovarian stimulation) in assisted reproductive technology programs
Triggering of final follicular maturation and ovulation (human chorionic gonadotropin) after adequate follicular development
Selected hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and stimulation of spermatogenesis in men (gonadotropins/hCG)

dosage.d: Start ~75-150 IU once daily; adjust by ~37.5-75 IU at intervals based on ovarian response
dosage.n: Individualize to follicular response; lowest effective dose to limit OHSS/multiples

dosage.d: 5,000-10,000 IU as a single dose (or recombinant hCG ~250 micrograms) when follicles are mature
dosage.n: Withhold if excessive ovarian response/very high estradiol (OHSS risk)

dosage.d: 50 mg once daily for 5 days, starting cycle day 3-5; may increase to 100 mg/day next cycle if no ovulation
dosage.t: Once daily x5 days per cycle
dosage.n: Usually limited to a few cycles; max 100 mg/day per label

dosage.d: 2.5 mg once daily for 5 days (may increase to 5-7.5 mg in subsequent cycles)
dosage.t: Once daily x5 days per cycle
dosage.n: Use for ovulation induction varies by region/approval (off-label in some); not for use in pregnancy

dosage.d: hCG (e.g., 1,000-2,000 IU 2-3 times weekly) +/- FSH/hMG, individualized
dosage.n: Long-term to stimulate testosterone and spermatogenesis

admin: Confirm the cause of infertility and exclude pregnancy, primary ovarian/testicular failure, untreated thyroid/adrenal dysfunction, hyperprolactinemia and tumors before starting
Individualize and titrate injectable gonadotropin doses to ovarian response using serial transvaginal ultrasound and serum estradiol
Administer FSH/hMG/hCG by the route specified for the product (subcutaneous or intramuscular); rotate injection sites
Withhold the hCG trigger and counsel/cancel the cycle if there is excessive ovarian response or markedly elevated estradiol (high OHSS risk)
Give oral agents (clomiphene/letrozole) as a fixed 5-day course early in the cycle; confirm ovulation and limit the number of treatment cycles
Counsel patients thoroughly about the risks of multiple pregnancy and OHSS and the need for monitoring
moa: Gonadotropins act directly on gonadal receptors: FSH stimulates ovarian granulosa-cell proliferation and follicular growth (and Sertoli-cell/spermatogenesis in men); LH and human chorionic gonadotropin act on theca and Leydig cells to stimulate androgen/steroid production, and an hCG bolus mimics the mid-cycle LH surge to trigger final oocyte maturation, ovulation and corpus luteum formation. Human menopausal gonadotropin provides combined FSH and LH activity. The oral ovulation stimulants act indirectly: clomiphene citrate is a selective estrogen-receptor modulator that blocks hypothalamic-pituitary estrogen receptors, removing negative feedback and increasing endogenous FSH and LH secretion to recruit follicles; letrozole is an aromatase inhibitor that lowers estrogen production, similarly increasing pituitary gonadotropin output and promoting follicular development.

absolute: Primary ovarian failure / high endogenous gonadotropins (gonadotropins will not work)
Uncontrolled thyroid or adrenal dysfunction, or hyperprolactinemia, until treated
Sex-hormone-dependent tumors or tumors of the hypothalamus/pituitary
Abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin; ovarian cysts/enlargement not due to PCOS
Known hypersensitivity to the specific agent; clomiphene/letrozole contraindicated in significant liver disease
relative: Polycystic ovary syndrome (heightened OHSS and multiple-follicle response)
Prior excessive ovarian response or OHSS
Thrombophilia or other thromboembolic risk factors
monitor: Serial transvaginal ultrasound (follicle number and size) and serum estradiol
Signs and symptoms of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
Multiple-pregnancy risk and cycle cancellation criteria

preg: Gonadotropins and ovulation stimulants are not for use during pregnancy and should be discontinued once pregnancy is confirmed; their purpose is to achieve conception. Clomiphene and letrozole are contraindicated in established pregnancy (potential fetal harm). There is an inherent increased risk of multiple pregnancy with these treatments.
lact: These agents are not indicated during breastfeeding. Gonadotropins are peptides unlikely to be absorbed orally by an infant, but treatment for infertility is not undertaken during lactation; oral agents should be avoided while nursing.
renal: Specific data are limited across the group; use with caution in renal impairment and individualize injectable dosing. Fluid shifts from OHSS can compromise renal function, so monitor in patients with reduced renal reserve.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment. Clomiphene citrate and letrozole are contraindicated or to be avoided in significant liver disease. Severe OHSS can be associated with hepatic dysfunction and should be monitored.

major: Other ovulation-stimulating agents - combined use increases OHSS and multiple-pregnancy risk; use only under specialist protocols
Tamoxifen / other SERMs with clomiphene - overlapping estrogen-receptor effects
moderate: GnRH agonists/antagonists - used together within ART protocols (intended), affecting gonadotropin requirements
Drugs affecting prolactin (e.g., dopamine antagonists) - may impair the response to ovulation induction
minor: No major routine drug-drug interactions for the injectable peptides outside reproductive co-medications
interactions.food: Oral agents may be taken with or without food; injectables are parenteral.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; general moderation advised when trying to conceive.
interactions.diagnostics: hCG cross-reacts with pregnancy tests (may give a false-positive shortly after a trigger injection); these agents alter serum estradiol, LH and FSH used for cycle monitoring.

serious: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can be severe with ascites, pleural effusion, hemoconcentration and thromboembolism
Visual disturbances (clomiphene) which may be persistent
rare: Possible association with ovarian neoplasia with prolonged use (uncertain)
emergency: Severe OHSS (rapid weight gain, severe abdominal distension/pain, breathlessness, reduced urine output)
Acute adnexal torsion or ovarian cyst rupture with hemodynamic compromise

monitoring: Serial transvaginal ultrasound for follicle number and size and serum estradiol during stimulation
Signs and symptoms of OHSS (weight, abdominal girth, dyspnea, urine output, hematocrit) during and after treatment
Cycle cancellation/coasting criteria when response is excessive
Confirmation of ovulation and early pregnancy with attention to multiple gestation
Visual symptoms with clomiphene; liver function where relevant
counsel: These treatments stimulate your ovaries to grow and release eggs; the dose is carefully adjusted using scans and blood tests
There is a real chance of twins or more - your team monitors this closely
Report severe bloating, rapid weight gain, severe tummy pain, breathlessness, or reduced urination urgently - this can mean overstimulation (OHSS)
With clomiphene, tell your doctor about any blurred vision or flashing lights and stop the drug
Take oral tablets for the exact 5 days you are told, and attend all monitoring scans/blood tests
Stop the medicine and contact your clinic once you know you are pregnant
pk: Follicular growth develops over days of injectable stimulation; ovulation ~36 hours after the hCG trigger
Clomiphene/letrozole oral Tmax within hours; hCG levels peak ~6-12 hours after IM injection
Varies by agent - hCG long (~24-36 h), FSH ~24-40 h, clomiphene ~5-7 days, letrozole ~2 days
Ovarian stimulation continues through the dosing course; hCG effect persists ~10-14 days (false-positive pregnancy tests)
Per individual product - many injectables refrigerated or room temperature; protect from light; oral tablets at room temperature
pearls: GROUP ENTRY - covers injectable FSH/LH/hMG and hCG plus oral ovulation stimulants (clomiphene, letrozole); always follow the specific product's approved label for exact dosing (FDA insert/EMA/WHO sources used here)
Two dominant risks across the whole group: ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and multiple pregnancy - mandate ultrasound + estradiol monitoring
Doses are individualized and titrated to ovarian response; withhold the hCG trigger if response is excessive
hCG triggers ovulation by mimicking the LH surge and can cause a false-positive pregnancy test for up to ~2 weeks
Clomiphene can cause visual disturbances - stop if these occur; letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) is an alternative oral inducer (regional approval varies)
Discontinue all agents once pregnancy is confirmed; counsel on thromboembolism and adnexal torsion warning signs
missed: For oral agents, if a dose in the 5-day course is missed, contact the clinic for advice rather than doubling up. For injectable gonadotropins, dosing is scheduled by the fertility team - report any missed injection promptly because it affects follicular timing and the trigger.
overdose: Excessive dosing or response leads to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome - the principal manifestation of overdose - with marked ovarian enlargement, ascites/effusions, hemoconcentration, electrolyte disturbance and risk of thromboembolism. Management is supportive: stop further stimulation, monitor fluid balance, hematocrit and electrolytes, provide thromboprophylaxis, manage ascites/effusions and hypovolemia, and hospitalize for severe cases. Oral-agent overdose is managed supportively.
